solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sweet-talk school governors demonstrating teaching aid

parts.note: flannel is British slang for smooth, flattering talk
a school's governing body is its board

explanation.surface: A school's governing body is wooed into showing off a new classroom gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: A flannel board is a cloth-covered board that felt shapes stick to, used in classrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth display board for sticking cut-out shapes is a classic classroom visual aid.

clue.text: Party in charity bazaar's giving out equal shares for all

indicators.note: the party word is placed inside the bazaar word, as the clue says it is in it

parts.note: a fair is a fete or bazaar, here with its possessive S
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Proceeds from a party at a charity bazaar are being shared out evenly.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair do's (or fair dos) is informal British for fair treatment, everyone getting an equal share.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase is an appeal for fairness, where everyone is treated alike and gets the same portion.

clue.text: Horrify a European after revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word for the European is read backwards

parts.note: a Lapp is a native of Lapland in northern Europe

explanation.surface: A European is appalled by the aftermath of a revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to shock or horrify them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Happy hour binge in one next door

indicators.note: happy in the sense of tipsy or merry suggests the letters reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone goes on a drinking binge during happy hour at the pub next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy' belongs with 'hour' in the surface, but it is the anagram signal for HOURBINGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbour is literally the person who lives in the next house.

clue.text: Star clue

definitions.meaning: the principal performer in a play or film
a hint or piece of evidence that guides an investigation

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a leading actor takes the lead, and a detective follows up a lead.

clue.text: Like some offices in unoccupied factory? Not entirely

parts.note: an open position or space is vacant, unoccupied

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a plant is an industrial factory

explanation.surface: An empty factory might be converted into modern offices, the question suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' removes the last letter T from PLANT, leaving PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-plan describes offices laid out as one large room without dividing walls.

clue.text: Dissident ordered beer, litres

indicators.note: ordered in the sense of arranged tells us to put the letters of beer into a new order

explanation.surface: A nonconformist at the bar orders litres of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like the dissident buying a drink at the bar, but it is the anagram signal; litres then follows as L.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel opposes authority, just as a dissident does, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Ignore flying doctor in the guise of Apache leader

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters of ignore scattering and landing in another order

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a common abbreviation for a doctor

explanation.surface: A flying doctor disregards a disguised chief of the Apache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' turns IGNORE into GERONI, followed by MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Geronimo was the famous nineteenth-century Apache war chief.

clue.text: Boy bagging trophy is very accurate

indicators.note: bagging means holding inside, so the trophy word goes within the boy word

parts.note: a son is a male child, a boy
a pot is informal for a cup or trophy in sport

explanation.surface: A lad who wins a trophy proves to be a very good shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on is informal for exactly right or precise.

clue.text: Elected soldier behind closed doors

parts.note: a candidate who has been elected is in
a private is the lowest-ranking soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is elected in a secret ballot held behind closed doors.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in private happens away from public view, behind closed doors.

clue.text: High-pitched signal that makes bishop jump, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word built here is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop; to leap is to jump

explanation.surface: A shrill electronic signal startles a bishop into leaping.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleep is a short high-pitched electronic tone, as from a pager.

clue.text: Daughter, one receiving unexpected help in ancient city

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the daughter and one letters hold the rest between them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: unexpected suggests the letters of help coming out in a surprising order

explanation.surface: A daughter gets unexpected help on a trip to an ancient Greek site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpected' looks like it describes the help received, but it signals the anagram, and 'receiving' has D and I hold it between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphi was an ancient Greek city, home of the famous oracle of Apollo.

clue.text: Make clear when one has short period abroad

parts.note: a spell is a short period of time
out means away from home, abroad

explanation.surface: Someone explains themselves after a short stint working overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell something out is to explain it plainly and in detail.

clue.text: Bar or car?

definitions.meaning: a bar, especially the lounge bar of a pub
in Britain a ... is a car with a closed body and separate boot

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a Wild West saloon serves drinks, and a saloon car is a family sedan.

clue.text: Check on work after meek and mild type makes something to eat

indicators.note: after means the check and work letters come behind the lamb word

parts.note: a lamb is the proverbial gentle, meek creature
CH is the chess abbreviation for check
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A gentle soul checks their work before cooking a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamb chop is a cut of meat, clearly something eaten.

clue.text: One identifies transmitter by name — Leo, perhaps

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them
Leo is an example of a star sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A radio station is identified by a name like Leo.
explanation.definitionFit: A call sign is the identifying code letters of a radio transmitter or station.

clue.text: Fail to get most important part and become discouraged

definitions.text: Fail to get most important part
definitions.meaning: the heart is the core of something, so missing it is losing the heart

explanation.definitionFit: Losing heart is an idiom for becoming dispirited, and literally means losing the central part.

clue.text: Radical annoyed humanitarian organisation

parts.note: red is used for a political radical or leftist
cross means irritated, annoyed

explanation.surface: A radical gets annoyed with a humanitarian charity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Cross is the international humanitarian relief organisation.

clue.text: Special firm used in Scottish town

indicators.note: special as in out of the ordinary signals the letters taking an unusual arrangement

explanation.surface: A specialist firm has been hired in a town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' looks like it describes the firm, but it is the anagram signal for FIRMUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumfries is a town in south-west Scotland.

clue.text: Talk about girl coming out at beginning of Easter

parts.note: a deb, debutante, is a girl making her formal entrance into society

indicators.note: beginning of means only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A girl makes her social debut at the start of Easter, giving people something to discuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming out' traditionally meant a debutante's first appearance in society.
explanation.definitionFit: To debate a subject is to discuss it, to talk about it.

clue.text: A horse exercised on the beach

indicators.note: exercised suggests the letters being worked and moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A horse is given a gallop along the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on land rather than at sea, so on the beach.

clue.text: Advocate has degree in English Language?

indicators.note: in means the degree letter is placed within the language word

parts.note: Norse is the language of medieval Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A barrister with a degree in English Language, the question implies.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a cause is to support or endorse it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Brigade's leader, close to guy shot accidentally

indicators.note: a leader is the one at the front, so the first letter of the word is used
close to means the end, so the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: a shot is an attempt or chance

explanation.surface: A man near the brigade commander is shot by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done by chance happens accidentally, without design.

clue.text: Greek character, the brightest star?

definitions.meaning: the first letter of the Greek alphabet
the brightest star in a constellation is given the first Greek letter, so a star pupil might be called this

explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first Greek letter and names the brightest star of each constellation.

clue.text: Cunning vixen died

parts.note: vixen and shrew both mean a bad-tempered, scolding woman

explanation.surface: A crafty female fox has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vixen' suggests the cunning fox, but here it is the shrewish woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd means astute and sharp-witted, close to cunning.

clue.text: More carried by Wessex Trains

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, so the letters are found within these words

explanation.surface: Extra passengers travel on a regional train service in Wessex.
explanation.walkthrough: Wessex Trains was a train company in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, more of something.

clue.text: Former PM, first to enter study

indicators.note: first to means the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: An ex-Prime Minister is the first to walk into the study.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden was British Prime Minister from 1955 to 1957.

clue.text: Miserable time for returning flock

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word for miserable is read backwards

parts.note: poor can mean miserable, pitiful or wretched

explanation.surface: A gloomy spell before the flock returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the whole run POOR plus T backwards; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a group or crowd, as is a flock.

clue.text: Great work of art, seldom seen abroad

indicators.note: abroad suggests the letters being scattered widely into a new order

explanation.surface: A masterpiece of art rarely shown outside its home country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' looks part of the definition, but it is fodder with SELDOM; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An old master is a great painting by a leading European artist of before about 1800.

clue.text: It's good for the petrol station, say, as daring step works

definitions.text: It's good for the petrol station, say

indicators.note: works as a verb means is worked over, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A bold move pays off for the garage forecourt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' reads as succeeds, but it is the anagram signal for ASDARINGSTEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing trade is custom from people who happen to go by, vital to a roadside garage.
